words.definition: A state of hardship, misfortune, or difficulty.
words.example: She showed great strength and resilience in the face of adversity.

words.definition: Dealing with things sensibly and realistically in a way that is based on practical rather than theoretical considerations.
words.example: A pragmatic approach to study scheduling ensures you cover all subjects before the exam.

words.definition: To make less severe, serious, or painful.
words.example: Reviewing daily flashcards helps mitigate the stress of exam preparation.

words.definition: Given to sudden and unaccountable changes of mood or behavior.
words.example: The administration was criticized for its capricious decision-making process.

words.definition: The expression or holding of opinions at variance with those previously or commonly held.
words.example: In a democracy, the right to peaceful dissent is a fundamental liberty.

words.definition: Involving many carefully arranged parts or details; detailed and complicated in design and planning.
words.example: The security system they installed was elaborate and highly effective.

words.definition: Possible to do easily or conveniently.
words.example: It is not feasible to complete the entire reviewer in a single afternoon.

words.definition: Excessively talkative, especially on trivial matters.
words.example: The garrulous witness took hours to explain a simple event to the court.

words.definition: A lengthy and aggressive speech.
words.example: They were subjected to a long harangue about their lack of discipline.

words.definition: About to happen; overhanging or threatening.
words.example: With the dark clouds gathering, rain seemed imminent.

words.definition: Open to more than one interpretation; ambiguous, uncertain, or questionable.
words.example: The politician gave an equivocal answer when asked about the proposed tax reforms.

words.definition: Showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise.
words.example: A meticulous review of the clerical questions can save you from spelling mistakes.

words.definition: Well-meaning and kindly; serving a charitable rather than a profit-making purpose.
words.example: The benevolent supervisor offered to mentor the new civil service interns.

words.definition: Feeling or expressing great happiness and triumph.
words.example: The reviewees were jubilant after receiving their passing results.

words.definition: A passionate expression of grief or sorrow; to mourn.
words.example: He lamented the fact that he did not start studying earlier in the year.

words.definition: New or unusual in an interesting or creative way.
words.example: She proposed a novel solution to speed up their numerical calculations.

words.definition: No longer produced or used; out of date.
words.example: The old classification rules became obsolete under the new memo guidelines.

words.definition: Engaged in, involving, or reflecting deep or serious thought.
words.example: She sat in a pensive mood, weighing her choices before taking the exam.

words.definition: A state of perplexity or uncertainty over what to do in a difficult situation.
words.example: He was in a quandary about whether to review clerical or verbal reasoning first.

words.definition: Able to withstand or recover quickly from difficult conditions.
words.example: A resilient study mindset will help you bounce back after low drill scores.

words.definition: Having knowledge or being aware of something.
words.example: Reviewees must be cognizant of the rules governing the examination rooms.

words.definition: Sharpness or severity; intellectual alertness or penetration.
words.example: Her mathematical acuteness helped her solve the complex numerical series instantly.

words.definition: Careful and persistent work or effort.
words.example: Your diligence in studying will pay off on the day of the Civil Service Exam.

words.definition: Examine or inspect closely and thoroughly.
words.example: You should scrutinize every option before selecting your final answer.

words.definition: Understood or implied without being stated directly.
words.example: There was a tacit agreement that everyone would remain silent during the mock exam.

words.definition: Present, appearing, or found everywhere.
words.example: Mobile phones have become ubiquitous in daily communications.

words.definition: Regard with great respect or revere.
words.example: Filipinos venerate historical figures who fought for national liberation.

words.definition: Feeling or showing caution about possible dangers or problems.
words.example: Be wary of questions that contain double negatives in the verbal section.

words.definition: Having or showing great zeal, passion, or enthusiasm.
words.example: The zealous instructor spent extra hours preparing mock reviews.

words.definition: Lasting for a very short time; transient.
words.example: Fame in the digital era is often ephemeral, lasting only a few days.
